subject: pharmacology
title: Antimalarials: ACT, severe artesunate, primaquine and prophylaxis

steps.tx: Chloroquine still cures sensitive vivax, ovale, and malariae malaria as a blood schizonticide, while **falciparum resistance** spread through the tropics and ended its reliable use there. Chronic cumulative use can cause **retinopathy** needing annual eye screening, cardiomyopathy, hypoglycaemia, and pruritus especially in dark skin, and rheumatology doses also need eye review. Overdose is rapidly dangerous with QT prolongation, seizures, and hypokalaemia, and chloroquine remains an old pregnancy safe standby when the parasite is sensitive to it.
steps.say: Chloroquine can still treat sensitive vivax malaria effectively in many regions. Falciparum parasites resisted it across most tropical regions. Long term use can damage the retina progressively. Eye screening detects toxicity before vision is lost. Overdose can threaten the heart and the brain very quickly indeed.

steps.tx: Artemisinin combination therapy clears falciparum malaria fast and protects the partner drug. **Artemether lumefantrine** runs three days and needs fatty food for absorption, DHA piperaquine prolongs QT, and artesunate amodiaquine can lower neutrophils, while vomiting after a dose may need redosing. **Kelch13** mutations cause delayed clearance in South East Asia and drive surveillance and debate about triple combinations. Weight bands dose children correctly, counterfeit drugs fail treatment, and ECG is selected when QT risk matters clinically.
steps.say: Combination therapy can clear falciparum parasites rapidly and reliably in patients. Lumefantrine absorbs better when taken with fatty food. A vomited dose may need to be repeated. Resistance markers now show delayed clearance in parts of Asia. Correct weight based dosing protects children from treatment failure.

steps.tx: Severe malaria is a medical emergency defined by cerebral disease, acidosis, hyperparasitaemia, renal failure, ARDS, or hypoglycaemia. **Intravenous artesunate** is superior to quinine because it clears parasites faster, works safer, and causes less hypoglycaemia, although delayed haemolysis can appear weeks later and needs watching. **Quinine** causes cinchonism, hypoglycaemia from insulin release, and QT prolongation and is used when artesunate is absent. Exchange transfusion is retired, fluids stay conservative in ARDS, and parasite density with lactate guides ICU care.
steps.say: Severe malaria can threaten the brain and the kidneys and the lungs. Intravenous artesunate clears parasites faster than quinine does. Delayed haemolysis may appear weeks after treatment ends. Quinine causes tinnitus and dangerous hypoglycaemia frequently. Intensive support treats complications while antiparasitic treatment works.

vis.caption: Severe Malaria Management: IV Artesunate is First-Line, with ICU Support

steps.tx: Primaquine finishes vivax and ovale malaria by killing liver hypnozoites and also sterilises falciparum gametocytes at single low dose. **Primaquine** causes haemolysis in G6PD deficiency so screening precedes radical cure, and it is banned in pregnancy, while **tafenoquine** offers single dose radical cure only after quantitative G6PD testing. Prophylaxis choices include doxycycline with sun sensitivity, mefloquine limited by vivid dreams and psychosis, and atovaquone proguanil which is safe but costly, chosen by resistance pattern and trip duration.
steps.say: Primaquine kills dormant liver forms that cause relapses. G6PD deficiency makes this drug haemolyse red cells dangerously. Pregnancy forbids primaquine because fetal status is unknown. Prophylaxis choices depend on resistance and adverse effects. Mefloquine is limited by neuropsychiatric adverse effects in many travellers.

steps.tx: This image shows a quantitative **G6PD test** analyser beside red cells containing Heinz bodies and bite cells, a liver hypnozoite panel, and a pregnancy ban symbol. It explains why primaquine and tafenoquine need G6PD testing before **radical cure** of vivax or ovale malaria, because oxidant haemolysis can be severe in deficiency. Exam questions pair hypnozoite eradication with haemolysis risk and pregnancy exclusion, so the test must come before the drug is prescribed.
steps.say: This image links G6PD testing with haemolysis and liver hypnozoites. The analyser measures enzyme activity before radical cure begins. Deficient red cells form Heinz bodies and bite cells under oxidant stress. Pregnancy excludes primaquine because fetal enzyme status remains unknown. Testing therefore protects the patient before the drug is given.
